content.user_title: Create Slack GIFs and Animated Emoji
content.value_statement: Slack GIFs and animated emoji must meet strict size and dimension limits. This skill provides reusable Python tools to design, optimize, and validate animations for Slack.
actual_capabilities: Creates GIF frames with reusable Python drawing and composition helpers.
Builds animations using bounce, shake, spin, pulse, fade, zoom, morph, slide, and other templates.
Validates GIF dimensions and file size against Slack message and emoji limits.
Optimizes GIF output with color quantization, duplicate frame removal, and emoji-focused settings.
Adds text outlines, palettes, particles, flashes, shadows, and easing effects to animations.
Provides example workflows for combining primitives into custom Slack reactions.
limitations: It requires Python image libraries such as Pillow, imageio, and numpy.
It does not upload GIFs to Slack or manage Slack workspace settings.
Complex emoji animations may still exceed the 64KB Slack emoji limit.
Emoji rendering quality depends on fonts available in the local environment.

use_cases.title: Design Team Reaction Assets
use_cases.description: Create polished Slack reaction GIFs that match a team color palette and fit Slack limits.

use_cases.title: Developer Team Status Emoji
use_cases.description: Generate small animated emoji for deploys, alerts, milestones, or incident updates.

use_cases.title: Community Event GIFs
use_cases.description: Build reusable celebration, reminder, and announcement animations for Slack channels.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Emoji
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a compact animated reaction.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Slack emoji GIF of a smiling face pulsing gently. Keep it under 64KB and validate the final file.

prompt_templates.title: Animate a Team Reaction
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with motion and text.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Slack message GIF where a rocket slides in, bounces once, and shows the word LAUNCHED with an outlined font.

prompt_templates.title: Combine Multiple Effects
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 480 by 480 Slack GIF that combines movement, impact flash, particles, and a short celebration loop.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize an Existing Idea
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced optimization for strict emoji constraints.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an animated warning emoji for Slack. Use 12 frames or fewer, 40 colors or fewer, and explain any optimization choices.

output_examples.input: Create a tiny animated emoji that says a task is blocked.
output_examples.output: A compact 128 by 128 GIF with a warning emoji pulsing twice, simple colors, and validation notes for Slack emoji size.

output_examples.input: Make a Slack GIF for a successful product launch.
output_examples.output: A 480 by 480 rocket animation with easing, confetti particles, outlined launch text, and size optimization for Slack messages.

output_examples.input: Create a funny reaction GIF for a surprise announcement.
output_examples.output: A short shake and zoom animation using emoji, impact flash, and reduced colors so the file remains Slack friendly.

best_practices: Validate dimensions and file size after each major animation change.
Use fewer frames and colors when creating Slack emoji GIFs.
Start with simple motion, then add effects only when they improve the message.
anti_patterns: Do not use long animations for Slack emoji because they often exceed 64KB.
Do not rely on gradients or many colors when strict compression is required.
Do not add small text that will be unreadable at emoji size.

faq.question: Can this skill create Slack custom emoji?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes emoji-focused settings and validators for Slack custom emoji constraints.

faq.question: Can it create larger message GIFs?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports larger Slack message GIFs, commonly around 480 by 480 pixels.

faq.question: Does it upload GIFs to Slack?
faq.answer: No. It creates and validates GIF files, but upload steps remain manual or external.

faq.question: What libraries does it need?
faq.answer: It uses Python image libraries including Pillow, imageio, imageio-ffmpeg, and numpy.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What happens if a GIF is too large?
faq.answer: The validators report size details and suggest reducing frames, colors, dimensions, or visual complexity.
